title: Laredo Health Promotores' Thanksgiving Drive Drew Dozens of Families in a Single Day
excerpt: The Laredo Health Promotores' Thanksgiving food drive drew 55 to 60 families in a single day of sign-ups.
content:
The Laredo Health Promotores' “Giving Thanks Giving Back” Thanksgiving Food Drive drew 55 to 60 families in a single day of sign-ups — a response the group's spokesperson called “outstanding” — as the coalition collected food to put Thanksgiving meals on tables across three of Laredo's ZIP codes.

The coalition collected food donations to provide Thanksgiving meals to families in need. Fifty-five to 60 families had already signed up when the drive was reported on Nov. 16, even though the registration form had been open for only one day. The first contribution came from a veteran on Veterans Day, Nov. 11. Requested donations included canned foods and vegetables, instant mashed potatoes, gravy, cranberry sauce, turkeys and nonperishable desserts, including Jell-O and Little Debbie snacks. Donations of all kinds were welcome. Donations were accepted at 1220 N. Malinche, at the Ruth B. Cowl Center, and meal distribution was scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21. For information, the coalition can be reached at 956-722-2431. Students could also earn community service hours by participating.

The coalition focuses on ZIP codes 78040, 78043 and 78046, where community needs assessments identified transportation as a significant challenge for residents seeking medical care. The Laredo Health Promotores was established following the 2023 Laredo City Needs Assessment and focuses on medical transportation, health education and connecting families to providers. Its partners include the City of Laredo Health Department, the Laredo Stroke Support Group, the Ruthe B. Cowl Rehabilitation Center and Mercy Ministries of Laredo.

The coalition received a $1.4 million Methodist Healthcare Ministries Prosperamos Juntos / Thriving Together grant over three years. Spokesperson A.J. Perales said the coalition is working toward becoming an official nonprofit and hopes to expand its services, including medical transportation.
